applicant_utility.summary: This is a partner-funded stipend of up to EUR 8,800 (Bachelor's) or EUR 17,600 (Master's) paid out over up to two years, so plan on it covering part of your study costs rather than the full price of studying in Graz. Master's applicants get the longer runway - the window runs 15 October 2026 to 15 February 2027 - while Bachelor's applicants must wait for the May-July 2027 window. Selection is two-stage: a TU Graz expert jury pre-selects, then the funding company or organisation makes the final decision, so your motivation letter should speak to both academic strength and fit with a named partner's field.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong final-year Bachelor's or recent graduates with top grades who want to start a TU Graz degree in winter semester 2027/28 and are willing to engage with a corporate sponsor.
application_readiness_checklist: Pick your target partner scholarship early and read its individual requirements, since sponsor conditions stack on top of TU Graz's general criteria
Ask your two referees for letters on official letterhead with signature early (Master's track) - this is the most common bottleneck
Merge everything into a single PDF set in German or English and keep file names clear and complete
Draft the motivation letter around specific, personal evidence rather than generic praise for TU Graz
Track the separate windows: Master's files by 15 February 2027, Bachelor's files by 7 July 2027
common_rejection_risks: Sponsor-specific criteria not met even though the general TU Graz criteria are (e.g. field-of-study fit, company-linked expectations)
Reference letters missing signature or official letterhead, or submitted in a language other than German or English
Weak or generic motivation letter - TU Graz explicitly asks for specific and personal content
Missing the one-window-per-year structure: the Master's and Bachelor's windows do not overlap and admit different cohorts
Assuming enrolment is required - admission is not needed at application, but the study must actually start in winter semester 2027/28
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: TU Graz publishes no tuition or living-cost coverage, so tuition fees, accommodation and daily living in Graz remain self-funded; treat the stipend as partial support only.
document_audit: Reference letters must be from teachers, on official letterhead, signed - photocopies or unsigned scans are a trap
Documents must arrive as PDFs in German or English; get translations certified before the window opens
Master's applicants should attach the Bachelor's diploma if it is already available and note that admission itself is not yet required
Bachelor's applicants need both the school-leaving certificate and the last school level's annual report with grades
alerts: Two different windows per year level - a late Master's application cannot be filed in the Bachelor's window
The final decision sits with the funding company, so stronger files are not automatically shortlisted by the TU Graz jury
For NAWI Graz programmes the main enrolment must be at TU Graz, not the partner university
Support runs up to two years, so budget for the remainder of your programme from other sources
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the PDF document set through TU Graz's application route inside the window, an expert jury pre-selects, and the scholarship donor makes the final award; awards are celebrated at an annual ceremony with the sponsors.

official.application_route: Apply via the Institute's online form during the annual call, then upload the full document set through the transfer link the Institute sends after the formal check.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship of a country in the Global South per the OECD DAC list and the Austrian government's continental classification (the FAQ lists all currently eligible countries); a student residence permit or student visa for Austria is also required.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is specifically for students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America studying in Salzburg.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Regular Master's or PhD programme at the University of Salzburg, UAS Salzburg or Mozarteum only. No scholarships for studies at private universities, postgraduate certificate programmes, blended-learning/distance courses without compulsory attendance in Austria, non-degree students, short-term visits or exchange programmes.
official.research_requirement: Doctoral students must submit confirmation of supervision and a detailed description of the research project with justification of its relevance to development policy.
official.duration: Scholarship contracts for a maximum of one academic year, extendable; the maximum funding period corresponds to the standard period of study plus one tolerance semester
official.description: The One World Scholarship of the Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg gives students from the Global South a partial scholarship of EUR 500 per month during the semester, combined with mentoring, a diverse educational programme and a global alumni network. The Institute awards a very limited number of places through a multi-stage process - online form, formal check, full application, online interview and a Grants Committee decision - and expects holders to engage actively in its programme.
official.program_type: Partial scholarship programme for international students from the Global South studying in Salzburg

applicant_utility.summary: This is a EUR 500-per-month partial stipend paid from October to June, so it eases rather than funds a Salzburg degree - but it comes with a tuition fee waiver at the University of Salzburg and UAS Salzburg, which is the real prize for fee-paying non-EU students. Only a very small number of places exist, so treat the June call as a race: the online form closes 12 July, full documents 15 July, interviews follow, and decisions land in early August. Plan around the hard eligibility filters - Global South citizenship from the Institute's country list, admission to a regular Salzburg Master's or PhD, a student residence permit or visa, and the age caps (30/35, 35/40 for mothers).
applicant_utility.best_fit: Global South citizens under the age caps who already hold admission to a regular Master's or PhD at Uni Salzburg, UAS Salzburg or Mozarteum, with demonstrated financial need and a development-focused field of study.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your country of citizenship against the Institute's published Global South list before investing in an application
Secure admission to a regular Salzburg programme and the student residence permit or visa first - applications without them are formally rejected
Prepare the whole document set in advance (degree certificates, transcripts, passport, 3 months of bank statements) so you can respond fast when the transfer link arrives
Record the 2-minute video early: who you are, why this field of study, and how you will contribute to the programme
Monitor aai-salzburg.at and the Institute's social channels from May, since the call opens only once a year and dates are not published far ahead
common_rejection_risks: Formal rejection before any content review: no admission yet, wrong residence title, age above the cap, or an ineligible programme type (private university, Lehrgang, distance learning, non-degree, exchange)
Documents not ready in time after the formal check - the Institute sends the transfer link with a short deadline
Weak financial-needs case: income, savings, parental support and other funding are all weighed
No demonstrable link between your studies and development-related issues
Little willingness to commit to monthly meetings and organising a programme event
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation and social security are explicitly not covered, and the EUR 500 monthly instalment is partial support only, so rent, insurance, food and transport in Salzburg remain self-funded.
document_audit: Degree certificates in languages other than English, French or Spanish need certified translations
Master's applicants need the Bachelor's thesis abstract; doctoral applicants need the supervision confirmation and a development-policy justification of the research project
Bank statements must cover the last 3 months - older statements are a common miss
The video is capped at 2 minutes; scripts longer than that get cut mid-answer
Joint Master's students must confirm eligibility with the Institute before applying, and funding covers only the period of study in Austria
alerts: The tuition fee waiver is currently confirmed only at the University of Salzburg and UAS Salzburg - Mozarteum students should not assume a waiver
Contracts run for one academic year at a time and can be extended, but never beyond the standard period of study plus one tolerance semester
Applying does not guarantee a place: positions are very limited and the whole cycle from form to decision closes within roughly two months
Funding is only paid for time physically spent studying in Austria
All correspondence runs through the e-mail address in the online form - watch the spam folder and follow up if nothing arrives within a week
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online form by 12 July, pass the formal-criteria check, upload the full document set via the transfer link for the 15 July full-application deadline, attend the online interview, and await the Grants Committee decision notified in the first half of August.
